LESSON: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Handwriting. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how to grasp a pencil, well?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use legible handwriting to communicate effectively
2. develop speed and ease of handwriting
3. acquire the skill of shaping different letters to write syllables, words, and sentences neatly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners practice activities that develop fine motor skills Links to PCIs: Life skills: Skills of knowing and living with others - effective communication Links to other learning areas: All learning areas improve the fine motor skills e.g. smearing mud, collecting materials for thatching

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use legible handwriting to communicate effectively
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use legible handwriting to communicate effectively. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. develop speed and ease of handwriting
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to develop speed and ease of handwriting. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. acquire the skill of shaping different letters to write syllables, words, and sentences neatly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners practice activities that develop fine motor skills Links to PCIs: Life skills: Skills of knowing and living with others - effective communication Links to other learning areas: All learning areas improve the fine motor skills e.g. smearing mud, collecting materials for thatching
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to acquire the skill of shaping different letters to write syllables, words, and sentences neatly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners practice activities that develop fine motor skills Links to PCIs: Life skills: Skills of knowing and living with others - effective communication Links to other learning areas: All learning areas improve the fine motor skills e.g. smearing mud, collecting materials for thatching. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Handwriting.
2. Explain Handwriting to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Handwriting.
4. Show that you can: use legible handwriting to communicate effectively
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Handwriting. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: how to grasp a pencil, well?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. use legible handwriting to communicate effectively
2. develop speed and ease of handwriting
3. acquire the skill of shaping different letters to write syllables, words, and sentences neatly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners practice activities that develop fine motor skills Links to PCIs: Life skills: Skills of knowing and living with others - effective communication Links to other learning areas: All learning areas improve the fine motor skills e.g. smearing mud, collecting materials for thatching

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
